task.title: Select the latest due recurrence occurrence
task.objective: Complete issue https://github.com/Knosence9/project-vela/issues/913 by selecting one exact finite recurrence's latest authored occurrence through a caller-owned inclusive cutoff.
acceptance_criteria: Use overflow-safe constant-space arithmetic and preserve exact identity, goal, instant, offset, and definition revision.
Return an unchanged cursor for a future starting coordinate and a null cursor only at finite completion.
Keep selection read-only and exclude ambient time, durable skip evidence, identity generation, materialization, and execution authority.

attempts.diagnostic: Focused recurrence-store tests failed because RecurrenceStore::latest_due_occurrence did not exist.
attempts.patch: Added tests for exact and between-instant cutoffs, future horizons, finite completion, nonzero starts, u64 boundaries, missing inputs, and a huge backlog before production behavior.

attempts.diagnostic: Added a typed exact-recurrence projection whose arithmetic selects the latest due authored offset without enumerating or allocating the backlog.
attempts.patch: Implemented latest_due_occurrence in crates/vela-kernel/src/scheduler.rs and documented the explicit latest-only catch-up contract in ADR-0060.

attempts.diagnostic: An initial CodeRabbit rate-limit result was rejected as false merge evidence. After cooldown, a genuine review completed with no actionable comments, zero review threads, and the exact head passed the Rust quality gate.
attempts.patch: Kept the API as one exact-recurrence typed projection rather than introducing a generic catch-up policy or mutation framework.

outcome.summary: The kernel can project the latest authored due occurrence in constant space while the caller retains cutoff, cursor, catch-up, persistence, identity, and execution policy.

lessons: Latest-only backlog collapse must be explicit in the API rather than hidden inside general due paging.
Closed-form indexed recurrence arithmetic avoids work proportional to a potentially huge backlog.
A returned continuation cursor is caller guidance, not durable skip, acceptance, or lifecycle evidence.
Read-only selection grants no persistence, task lifecycle, dispatch, retry, permission, workflow, provider, tool, or execution authority.
A successful review status that reports rate limiting is not substantive review evidence.
